answer: Neighborhood Closure Credit. Each identity's reach is capped by the number of distinct agents that mutually transact with it and with each other, forming a closed grove of verified edges. An agent whose counterparties don't interconnect gets no outward routing weight, so fake clusters stay isolated. Reaching useful traffic share forces an attacker to build real two-way links toward the network's zenith, costing genuine interaction volume per identity. Lotus identities can't shortcut this: sparse links mean near-zero influence.
